      "title": "The review store",
      "body": "Every `submit-review` that reads a document writes it down: a clean review\nas a review, a failing input as a rejected input, in separate trees, never\nmixed, so the store answers \"what was concluded about this commit\" without\na failure polluting it. Exit 3 is the exception: it records a row and\nwrites no file.\n\nStoring needs no flag: it is simply what `submit-review` always does.\n`store.enabled: false` in the config file is the only way to turn it off.\nThe result object never mentions where a copy landed — that is\n`loam-refinery reviews`'s job.\n\nResubmitting under the same profile supersedes rather than replaces: it\nadds a new row. `collect-reviews` marks the earlier one `superseded_by` and\nrequalifies its ids from `profile:id` to `#N:id`, so an id from an earlier\ncollect can stop resolving.\n\nA store that cannot be created or written — read-only home, full disk,\nunreachable `store.path` — exits 101: the machine is at fault, not the\nreview.     {
      "name": "tiers",
      "namespace": "topic",
      "title": "Check tiers and exit codes",
      "body": "Checks come in three tiers answering different questions.\n\nStructural checks ask \"is this a document?\" — schema conformance, unique ids,\nsafe paths, well-formed refs. Always run, always hard.\n\nVerification checks ask \"is this about anything real?\" — does this path exist at\nthis ref, does the file have this many lines. Always run, and cannot be\ndisabled or demoted: an anchor claim that goes unconfirmed fails the run.\n\nAdvisory checks ask \"is this a good review?\" — a thin body, a suggestion with no\nstated cost, every comment at priority 9. Always run, never fatal.\n--strict promotes them to errors; no flag silences one.\n\nExit 0 is valid, exit 1 means revise the review, exit 2 means fix the\ninvocation, exit 3 means the reviewed state is not a commit — commit it, or\nrun `git stash create` and submit that SHA — and exit 101 means the tool\nfailed: stop and report the machine. Document-unparseable and exit 3 both\ngate the rest; every other run reports everything findable, skipped checks\nincluded.",

      "name": "verification",
      "namespace": "topic",
      "title": "Anchors as checkable claims",
      "body": "An anchor says: this path, at this commit, has this line. That is a factual\nclaim, and the one an agent gets wrong most confidently: a hallucinated line\nnumber is well-formed, plausibly numbered, and wrong.\n\nSo the document carries a ref: a full 40-character commit SHA, never a branch.\nA branch names a moving target — an anchor recorded against main means whatever\nmain points at when someone looks, stale without ever changing.\n\nsubmit-review checks those claims against the repository it is run in, by default\nand with no flag, by object lookup — a commit that is not checked out still\nresolves. With no repository the tier is skipped, reported as skipped —\nbut not passed: any anchor still fails at exit 1 with nothing to confirm it.\nAn anchorless document passes either way.\n\nloam-refinery confirms the anchor points somewhere; whether it points at\nthe right line is the reviewer's job. What the SHA buys is that anyone can\ncheck:\n\n  git show 4f2c1a9:internal/fetch/client.go | sed -n '88,94p'",
